## 1 · Package pins re-cut — verified against the real bookworm pool

The R6.32 blocker (`Blocked{backend.package_pins_unavailable}`) was a
planning defect: the pin cut anticipated versions older than what the
declared image's apt sources offer. Re-cut against the current
`deb.debian.org/debian bookworm` pool, verified inside a
`debian:bookworm` container **on amd64** (the declared `e2-standard-8`
architecture — binNMU `+bN` suffixes are arch-specific, so the arm64
check alone would not be honest evidence):

```
$ docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 debian:bookworm bash -c \
    'apt-get update -qq && for p in podman crun conmon netavark \
     podman-compose; do apt-cache policy $p; done'
podman:          Candidate: 4.3.1+ds1-8+deb12u1+b3   (bookworm/main amd64)
crun:            Candidate: 1.8.1-1+deb12u1          (bookworm/main amd64)
conmon:          Candidate: 2.1.6+ds1-1              (bookworm/main amd64)
netavark:        Candidate: 1.4.0-3                  (bookworm/main amd64)
podman-compose:  Candidate: 1.0.3-3                  (bookworm/main all)
```

Simulated pinned install (the exact argv `startup.sh` will run):

```
$ docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 debian:bookworm bash -c \
    'apt-get update -qq && apt-get -s install -y --allow-downgrades \
     podman=4.3.1+ds1-8+deb12u1+b3 crun=1.8.1-1+deb12u1 conmon=2.1.6+ds1-1 \
     netavark=1.4.0-3 podman-compose=1.0.3-3'
Inst netavark (1.4.0-3 Debian:12.15/oldstable [amd64])
Inst conmon (2.1.6+ds1-1 Debian:12.15/oldstable [amd64])
Inst crun (1.8.1-1+deb12u1 Debian:12.15/oldstable [amd64])
Inst podman (4.3.1+ds1-8+deb12u1+b3 Debian:12.15/oldstable [amd64])
Inst podman-compose (1.0.3-3 Debian:12.15/oldstable [all])
```

All five pins resolve — the offers match the VM-observed repo versions
recorded in runs/R6.32.md exactly. No snapshot-mirror source needed; the
closed schema is untouched. The amd64 check matters: `+b3` is a per-arch
binary-NMU suffix (arm64 also shows `+b3` for podman here, verified
separately — recorded for completeness, amd64 is the declared arch).

## 2 · `startup-script` landing — diagnosis + repair

**What landed (R6.32 live evidence):** the provisioned instance's
metadata carried `hh_deadman_minutes` + `hh_packages` but not
`startup-script`; the guest journal reported "No startup scripts to
run". The committed script ran in-guest over SSH instead.

**Reproduced argv** (from the committed provision receipt
`2026-11-09-fp-w1-provision.json`):

```
gcloud compute instances create hh-fp-w1 … \
  --metadata "hh_deadman_minutes=735" \
  --metadata-from-file "startup-script=<…>/scripts/gce-backend/startup.sh" \
  --metadata-from-file "hh_packages=<…>/packages.txt" \
  …
```

**Mechanism:** two `--metadata-from-file` occurrences. gcloud parses
each occurrence as the complete file-backed metadata map — the second
occurrence (`hh_packages=…`) replaced the first (`startup-script=…`), so
the key never reached instance metadata. The keys that landed are
exactly the last occurrence's map plus the separate inline `--metadata`
entry — matching the observed state precisely. The documented form is
one flag with a comma-separated `KEY=FILE,[KEY=FILE,…]` list
(`gcloud compute instances create` flag reference).

**Repair** (`scripts/gce-backend.sh` `cmd_provision`): the two
occurrences merged into one —

```
--metadata "hh_deadman_minutes=$DMIN" \
--metadata-from-file "startup-script=$STARTUP,hh_packages=$TMPD/packages.txt"
```

with a comment in-source recording the R6.32 drop. Size is no factor
(startup.sh ≈ 2.3 KB ≪ the 256 KB per-value metadata bound); escaping is
no factor (file paths carry no commas).

**Test:** `scripts/check-gce-backend.sh` §4 gains three legs — (a)
exactly one `--metadata-from-file` occurrence in the create argv, (b)
both `startup-script=` and `hh_packages=` as top-level comma-separated
elements of that one argv, (c) `hh_deadman_minutes` still under the
inline `--metadata`. The battery pins the argv so a regression to two
occurrences fails deterministically, fixture-verified — the live landing
itself is what GATE-G33's PROV-W1 re-run will show.
